facts.text: Pacifica was officially incorporated in 1957, merging nine small coastal communities into one city.
The city’s roots trace back to the 1769 Portolà expedition, which first sighted San Francisco Bay from Sweeney Ridge.
During World War II, the area now known as Sharp Park housed a detention station that processed Japanese Americans and other foreign nationals.
The Pacifica Historical Society runs the Coastside Museum, where visitors can see a working model of the short‑lived Ocean Shore Railroad.
Pacifica’s cultural scene thrives around the Pacifica Arts Center, which partners with the Historical Society to promote local arts and heritage.
The city’s name, meaning “peaceful” in Spanish, reflects its calm coastal setting between San Francisco and Half Moon Bay.
